Using the **tabular method**, I differentiate $x^5$ repeatedly and integrate $\sin(3x)$ repeatedly:

| Derivatives of $x^5$ | Integrals of $\sin(3x)$ | Sign |
|---|---|---|

| $120x$ | $\frac{1}{81}\sin(3x)$ | − |
| $120$ | $-\frac{1}{243}\cos(3x)$ | + |

## Combining Terms

$$\int x^5\sin(3x)\,dx = -\tfrac{1}{3}x^5\cos(3x) + \tfrac{5}{9}x^4\sin(3x) + \tfrac{20}{27}x^3\cos(3x) - \tfrac{20}{27}x^2\sin(3x) - \tfrac{40}{81}x\cos(3x) + \tfrac{40}{243}\sin(3x)$$

Multiplying by $-1$ (since the original integrand has a leading minus sign):

## Verification

Differentiating the result gives:
- $\sin(3x)$ terms: $-x^5$ (all others cancel)
- $\cos(3x)$ terms: all cancel

Result: $-x^5\sin(3x)$ ✓
